title: Derangement reciprocal-product congruences
statement:
For a positive integer $n$, let $D(n)=\{\tau\in S_n:\tau(j)\ne j\text{ for all }j=1,\ldots,n\}$ be the set of derangements, and let $\operatorname{sign}(\tau)$ denote the sign of a permutation. **Derangement congruences.** For any odd prime $p$,

$$
\sum_{\tau\in D(p-1)}\prod_{j=1}^{p-1}\frac{1}{j-\tau(j)}\equiv\left(\frac{-1}{p}\right)\pmod{p^2}
$$

and

$$
\sum_{\tau\in D(p-1)}\operatorname{sign}(\tau)\prod_{j=1}^{p-1}\frac{1}{j-\tau(j)}\equiv1\pmod{p^2}.
$$

These congruences concern derangement-restricted permanent- and determinant-type sums; the supplied text gives no resolution.
source_name: Zhi-Wei Sun, “On some determinants and permanents”, arXiv:2207.13039 (2024).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.13039

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2022).
